accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the National Green Tribunal (NGT)?
o: It is a constitutional body established under Article 21
It is a statutory body established under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010
It is a quasi-judicial body established under Article 323B
It is an executive body established under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986
accepted.x: The NGT is a statutory body established under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010. It is not a constitutional body.
accepted.tq: Distinguish statutory bodies from constitutional bodies and check the parent law.
accepted.sec: National Green Tribunal - Act, date, constitutional basis, benches, composition, Acts covered, appeal

accepted.s: The National Green Tribunal gives effect to the right to a healthy environment primarily as a part of which constitutional provision?
accepted.x: The right to a healthy environment has been treated as part of the right to life under Article 21.
accepted.tq: Match the right with its correct constitutional article.
accepted.sec: National Green Tribunal - Act, date, constitutional basis, benches, composition, Acts covered, appeal

accepted.s:
With reference to the composition of the National Green Tribunal, consider the following statements:
1. It has a Chairperson who is a retired Judge of the Supreme Court.
2. It includes Judicial Members and Expert Members.
3. There are 10 to 20 Judicial Members and 10 to 20 Expert Members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The NGT consists of a Chairperson who is a retired Supreme Court judge, along with Judicial and Expert Members, with 10 to 20 members in each category.
accepted.tq: Verify the composition by separating the chairperson, member categories and numerical range.
accepted.sec: National Green Tribunal - Act, date, constitutional basis, benches, composition, Acts covered, appeal

accepted.s:
Which of the following Acts is outside the scope of the National Green Tribunal as specified in its jurisdictional list?
1. Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972
2. Forest Rights Act
3. Biological Diversity Act, 2002
4. Environment (Protection) Act, 1986
accepted.x: The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 and the Forest Rights Act are outside the stated scope. The Biological Diversity Act, 2002 and the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 are covered Acts.
accepted.tq: Use exclusion testing to distinguish covered Acts from Acts outside the specified scope.
accepted.sec: National Green Tribunal - Act, date, constitutional basis, benches, composition, Acts covered, appeal

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs of Acts is correctly matched with the Acts covered by the National Green Tribunal?
1. Water Act, 1974
2. Air Act, 1981
3. Biological Diversity Act, 2002
4. Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991
accepted.x: All four listed Acts are among the Acts covered by the NGT. The original Schedule I also included the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991.
accepted.tq: Check the complete statutory list rather than stopping at the commonly cited environmental Acts.
accepted.sec: National Green Tribunal - Act, date, constitutional basis, benches, composition, Acts covered, appeal

accepted.s: Which one of the following Acts was included in the original Schedule I of the National Green Tribunal framework?
accepted.x: The Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991 was included in the original Schedule I. The Wildlife (Protection) Act and the Forest Rights Act are outside the stated scope.
accepted.tq: Use a less frequently recalled item from the statutory list as the correct option.
accepted.sec: National Green Tribunal - Act, date, constitutional basis, benches, composition, Acts covered, appeal

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below.

List-I (NGT location)
a. Principal Bench
b. Zonal Bench

d. Zonal Bench

List-II (Location)

option_a: a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Ban on rat-hole mining in Meghalaya — Unscientific and unsafe coal mining
2. Art of Living fine — Damage to the Yamuna floodplain
3. Ban on diesel vehicles older than 10 years in Delhi-NCR — Air pollution
4. Direction to BRO to plant trees — Tree felling for road works
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched with the respective NGT orders and issues.
accepted.tq: Match each landmark order with its underlying environmental issue.
accepted.sec: NGT landmark orders → issue

accepted.s: The National Green Tribunal’s order relating to rat-hole mining in Meghalaya was principally concerned with:
o: Air pollution caused by diesel vehicles
accepted.x: The 2014 ban on rat-hole mining in Meghalaya addressed unscientific and unsafe coal mining.
accepted.tq: Use the issue rather than the date to identify the landmark order.
accepted.sec: NGT landmark orders → issue

accepted.s: The Art of Living was fined by the National Green Tribunal in connection with damage to the:
o: Yamuna floodplain during the World Culture Festival
accepted.x: The 2016 order concerned damage to the Yamuna floodplain during the World Culture Festival.
accepted.tq: Link the organisation and event to the affected environmental site.
accepted.sec: NGT landmark orders → issue

accepted.s: The National Green Tribunal’s ban on diesel vehicles older than 10 years in Delhi-NCR was primarily related to:
accepted.x: The 2015 Delhi-NCR order concerning diesel vehicles older than 10 years addressed air pollution.
accepted.tq: Identify the environmental issue directly associated with the order.
accepted.sec: NGT landmark orders → issue

accepted.s: Under which provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 are the NCLT and NCLAT respectively set up?
accepted.x: NCLT is established under Section 408 and NCLAT under Section 410 of the Companies Act, 2013.
accepted.tq: Check the order of the statutory provisions instead of treating the two tribunals as interchangeable.
accepted.sec: NCLT/NCLAT - parent Act, adjudicating authority under IBC, appeal route

accepted.s:
The National Company Law Tribunal replaced which of the following bodies?
1. Company Law Board
2. Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction
3. Appellate Authority for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction
4. Securities Appellate Tribunal
accepted.x: NCLT replaced the Company Law Board, BIFR and AAIFR. It did not replace the Securities Appellate Tribunal.
accepted.tq: Use the replaced-body list and reject the unrelated appellate tribunal.
accepted.sec: NCLT/NCLAT - parent Act, adjudicating authority under IBC, appeal route

accepted.s: Which authority is the adjudicating authority for corporate insolvency under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016?
accepted.x: The NCLT is the adjudicating authority for corporate insolvency under the IBC, 2016. The DRT is the authority for individuals and partnership firms.
accepted.tq: Ask which body would handle the dispute by distinguishing corporate from individual insolvency.
accepted.sec: NCLT/NCLAT - parent Act, adjudicating authority under IBC, appeal route

accepted.s: For individuals and partnership firms under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, the adjudicating authority is the:
accepted.x: For individuals and partnership firms, the Debt Recovery Tribunal is the adjudicating authority. Corporate insolvency is handled by the NCLT.
accepted.tq: Apply the corporate-versus-non-corporate distinction to identify the correct forum.
accepted.sec: NCLT/NCLAT - parent Act, adjudicating authority under IBC, appeal route

accepted.s: Resolution plans under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code are expected to be completed within approximately:
accepted.x: Resolution plans are expected within 180 to 330 days.
accepted.tq: Use the stated range and reject options that shift either its lower or upper limit.
accepted.sec: NCLT/NCLAT - parent Act, adjudicating authority under IBC, appeal route

accepted.s:
Which of the following bodies are among those from which the NCLAT hears appeals?
1. NCLT
2. Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India
3. Competition Commission of India
4. National Financial Reporting Authority
accepted.x: NCLAT hears appeals from the NCLT, IBBI, CCI and NFRA under the specified provisions and dates.
accepted.tq: Test the full appellate-source list rather than only the most familiar source.
accepted.sec: NCLT/NCLAT - parent Act, adjudicating authority under IBC, appeal route

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the correct route of appeal from the National Company Law Tribunal?
accepted.x: Appeals from the NCLT lie to the NCLAT, and a further appeal lies to the Supreme Court.
accepted.tq: Follow the institutional hierarchy before identifying the final appellate court.
accepted.sec: NCLT/NCLAT - parent Act, adjudicating authority under IBC, appeal route

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the bench structure of the NCLAT?
o: Principal Bench at New Delhi and benches at Hyderabad and Kolkata only
A single bench functioning only at New Delhi
Principal Bench at New Delhi and a bench at Chennai
Principal Bench at Mumbai and benches at Bhopal and Pune
accepted.x: The NCLAT has its Principal Bench at New Delhi and another bench at Chennai.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the NCLAT bench locations from those of the NGT and NCLT.
accepted.sec: NCLT/NCLAT - parent Act, adjudicating authority under IBC, appeal route

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Articles 323A and 323B:
1. Article 323A deals with recruitment and service conditions of public servants.
2. Article 323A permits Parliament and State Legislatures to legislate equally.
3. Article 323B covers subjects such as taxation, foreign exchange and industrial disputes.
4. Article 323B permits a hierarchy of tribunals.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Under Article 323A, Parliament alone can legislate; therefore, statement 2 is false.
accepted.tq: Separate the legislative competence and hierarchy rules before selecting the code.
accepted.sec: Tribunals under Articles 323A and 323B - amendment and subjects

accepted.s: The provision relating to rent and tenancy rights was added to Article 323B by the:
accepted.x: Clause (h) relating to rent and tenancy rights was added to Article 323B by the 75th Amendment Act, 1993.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the amendment that inserted the Articles from the later amendment adding a subject.
accepted.sec: Tribunals under Articles 323A and 323B - amendment and subjects

accepted.s:
Which of the following is a feature of tribunals under Article 323A?
1. One tribunal for the Centre and one for each State or group of States
2. No hierarchy of tribunals
3. Legislation by Parliament only
4. Jurisdiction over elections and foodstuffs
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 describe Article 323A. Elections and foodstuffs are subjects associated with Article 323B, so statement 4 is false.
accepted.tq: Separate the subject list of Article 323B from the institutional features of Article 323A.
accepted.sec: Tribunals under Articles 323A and 323B - amendment and subjects

accepted.s:
The Central Administrative Tribunal has original jurisdiction over service disputes involving:
1. Central civil servants
2. Officers of the All-India Services
3. Civilian defence employees
4. All private-sector employees
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: CAT has original jurisdiction over service disputes of Central civil servants, All-India Services officers and civilian defence employees. It does not have general jurisdiction over all private-sector employees.
accepted.tq: Reject the overbroad jurisdictional statement and identify the specified categories.
accepted.sec: Central Administrative Tribunal - parent Act, jurisdiction, appeal route

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the composition and bench structure of the Central Administrative Tribunal?
o: Main Bench at New Delhi, 18 benches and 69 members comprising 35 Judicial and 34 Administrative Members
Main Bench at Mumbai, 16 benches and 69 members comprising 34 Judicial and 35 Administrative Members
Main Bench at New Delhi, 18 benches and 69 members comprising 34 Judicial and 35 Administrative Members
Main Bench at New Delhi, 20 benches and 69 members comprising 35 Judicial and 34 Administrative Members
accepted.x: CAT has its main bench at New Delhi and 18 benches. It has 69 members: 35 Judicial Members, including the Chairperson, and 34 Administrative Members.
accepted.tq: Check the location, number of benches, total strength and category-wise split together.
accepted.sec: Central Administrative Tribunal - parent Act, jurisdiction, appeal route

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about the Central Administrative Tribunal is correct?
1. It is bound by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 in all proceedings.
2. Its orders are subject first to appeal before a High Court Division Bench.
3. A further appeal lies to the Supreme Court.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: CAT is not bound by the CPC, 1908. Following the judicial review ruling, its orders go first to a High Court Division Bench and then to the Supreme Court.
accepted.tq: Combine the procedural rule with the post-review appellate route.
accepted.sec: Central Administrative Tribunal - parent Act, jurisdiction, appeal route

accepted.s: The decision in L. Chandra Kumar (1997) is associated with which of the following?
o: Creation of the Central Administrative Tribunal under Article 323A
Transfer of corporate insolvency jurisdiction from NCLT to DRT
Exclusion of all judicial review by High Courts over tribunal orders
Striking down exclusion clauses and affirming judicial review under Articles 32 and 226 as part of the basic structure
accepted.x: L. Chandra Kumar struck down the exclusion clauses in Articles 323A(2)(d) and 323B(3)(d), holding that judicial review under Articles 32 and 226 is part of the basic structure.
accepted.tq: Associate the landmark case with its precise constitutional consequence.
accepted.sec: Central Administrative Tribunal - parent Act, jurisdiction, appeal route

accepted.s: Which one of the following cases had upheld judicial review before the decision in L. Chandra Kumar, according to the stated judicial history?
accepted.x: The earlier S.P. Sampath Kumar case of 1987 also upheld judicial review in the context of tribunals.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the earlier case in the judicial sequence from the later constitutional ruling.
accepted.sec: Central Administrative Tribunal - parent Act, jurisdiction, appeal route

accepted.s: The Securities Appellate Tribunal was set up under the:
o: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 1999
accepted.x: The Securities Appellate Tribunal was established under the SEBI Act, 1992.
accepted.tq: Identify the parent statute rather than one of the regulators whose orders it reviews.
accepted.sec: Securities Appellate Tribunal - appeals from which regulators

accepted.s:
The Securities Appellate Tribunal hears appeals against orders of:
1. SEBI
2. IRDAI
3. PFRDA
4. CCI
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: SAT hears appeals against orders of SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA. Appeals against CCI orders lie to the NCLAT, not SAT.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the regulator-wise appellate jurisdiction of SAT from that of NCLAT.
accepted.sec: Securities Appellate Tribunal - appeals from which regulators

accepted.s: An appeal against a decision of the Securities Appellate Tribunal to the Supreme Court lies on:
accepted.x: A SAT decision can be appealed to the Supreme Court on points of law.
accepted.tq: Identify the legally limited ground of further appeal.
accepted.sec: Securities Appellate Tribunal - appeals from which regulators
